page: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an instance within the Optimized Cloud Compute family, equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core on an AMD EPYC processor operating at 2.0 GHz. The CPU leverages x86_64 architecture with 32 MB of L3 cache, standard vector instruction support via AVX, and dedicated hardware cryptographic features including AES and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 16.0 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a 200 GB local NVMe solid-state drive along with one complimentary public IPv4 address. It contains no discrete graphics hardware.

Benchmark testing highlights pronounced single-core execution alongside typical limitations of a low-core envelope. The server achieved top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng with 3135.07 operations and a strong Geekbench single-core score of 2123.0. Multi-core performance remains constrained by the dual-thread ceiling, registering 6221.86 in stress-ng and a multi-core score of 3800.0 in Geekbench. In memory testing, uncached large-block throughput recorded 73.36 GB/sec for reads and 52.37 GB/sec for writes. Application-level metrics reflect low parallel capacity, with Redis SET operations at 4.84 million per second and static web serving throughput at 2.14 GB/sec.

Because of its 1:8 core-to-memory ratio, the configuration is cost-effective for operational patterns where working dataset footprint outpaces computational demands. The bundled 200 GB NVMe storage provides local I/O capacity, though workloads demanding extensive parallel compilation, ray tracing, or heavy multi-tenant web traffic will encounter thread saturation. The instance fits lightweight relational databases, in-memory caching nodes, small data processing queues, staging servers, and background utilities with modest multi-threading needs.
description: Vultr voc-m-2c-16gb-200s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute instance built on x86_64 AMD EPYC processors running at 2.0 GHz. It pairs 2 dedicated vCPUs on a single physical core with 16.0 GB of memory and a 200 GB NVMe SSD, lacking discrete GPUs. Benchmark results reveal strong single-thread capability, with top-tier stress-ng single-core performance and strong Geekbench single-core scores, whereas aggregate multi-core throughput remains limited by the two-thread ceiling. Memory subsystem benchmarks show moderate transfer rates, including 73.36 GB/sec large-block reads and 52.37 GB/sec writes. The generous 8.0 GB RAM per vCPU allocation provides high memory capacity relative to compute footprint, making this configuration cost-efficient for memory-bound tasks with modest CPU requirements. It is well-fitted for lightweight databases, in-memory caching tiers, staging environments, and single-threaded data processing, but less suited for high-throughput static web hosting or multi-threaded build jobs.
